items.title: Beige Book — November 25, 2026 (Chicago District and national)
items.summary: Chicago District: Economic activity in the Seventh District was unchanged overall in October and early November, similar to the assessment in the prior reporting period. Contacts expected a slight decrease over the coming year. Manufacturing demand rose modestly; employment was up slightly; consumer spending was flat on balance; construction and real estate activity and business spending declined modestly; and nonbusiness contacts saw no change in economic activity. Prices rose moderately, wages rose modestly, and financial conditions tightened modestly. Farm income expectations for 2026 edged lower. National: Eight of the twelve Federal Reserve Districts reported growth in the slight to moderate range, while four Districts reported no change. Consumer spending was little changed, as households remained price sensitive and were increasingly selective in discretionary purchases. Tourism and travel activity was solid while entertainment and hospitality spending was mixed overall. Auto sales softened, which contacts attributed to elevated fuel prices and higher interest rates. Residential real estate activity weakened as affordability challenges suppressed demand, while commercial real estate activity was mixed. Construction activity declined amid higher borrowing costs and elevated construction costs. Manufacturing activity grew modestly overall, as robust demand in several industrial segments offset weakness in consumer-facing and housing-related goods. Overall transportation activity grew modestly despite uneven demand, persistent capacity and infrastructure constraints, and rising cost pressures. Port volumes were slightly lower due to weather-driven disruptions, even as data center–related imports rose. Energy activity grew modestly but investment in this sector remained restrained by elevated geopolitical, policy, and cost uncertainties. Banking conditions were little changed overall, as loan demand remained subdued, while nonfinancial services activity increased slightly. High costs for housing and other essentials strained household budgets, increased demand for social services, and stretched nonprofit capacity. Overall, the majority of Districts expected slight to moderate growth.
